newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso shuns rates fall to close firmer.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso shuns rates fall to close firmer.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed earlier softness to close slightly firmer against the dollar on Wednesday despite sharp falls in primary interest rates, traders said.
"They were expecting the peso to slide after the plunge in primary rates, but as volume was thin and the market quiet, dealers stepped in to sell dollars," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.7 and 0.6 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.8600/7.8640 and 7.8590/7.8620 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.95 of a centavo weaker at 7.8700/7.8730 per dollar.
Rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes fell 238 basis points to 20.23 percent at Banco de Mexico's weekly primary auction on Tuesday night.

"We are not fully aware of what happened; there were dollars everywhere," another trader said. "Someone sold a long dollar position or a broker trading on behalf of a corporation probably prompted the market to sell dollars."
Dealers said the peso could break resistance at 7.86 per dollar on Thursday following stronger-then-expected trade balance figures released in late trade.

The Finance Ministry announced Mexico had notched up a preliminary trade surplus of $565 million in March, compared with an average forecast of $3324.29 million in a Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses.
